tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. address `addr` and the provenance `prov`; `decode` reads an address back from a representation and
reads only its first `size` bytes. -/
structure PtrEnc where
  /-- §82.3: number of bytes of a reference. -/
  size : Nat
  /-- §82.3, §10 ¶4: byte `i` of the reference to `addr` with provenance `prov`. -/
  enc : Nat → Option Nat → Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat
  /-- §82.3: the address read back from a representation. -/
  decode : (Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) → Nat
  /-- `decode` reads only the first `size` bytes of a representation (§82.3, §81 Spec 11). -/
  reads : ∀ f g, (∀ i, i < size → f i = g i) → decode f = decode g

/-- Obligation of the encoding for a reference to `addr` with provenance `prov` (§82.3; Spec 11,
§81: address width and encodings are not fixed here): it decodes back to `addr` and every byte
carries the provenance `prov` (§10 ¶4). -/
def PtrEncAt (pe : PtrEnc) (addr : Nat) (prov : Option Nat) : Prop :=
  pe.decode (pe.enc addr prov) = addr ∧ ∀ i, (pe.enc addr prov i).2 = prov

/-- The allocation of the effective anchor of authority `a` (§44; §82.2: the provenance of a
reference to the region of `a`): the allocation of the root authority reached along its origin
chain, read on the first leaf of its footprint. -/
def anchorAlloc (L : Layout) (s3 : S3) (a : Nat) : Nat :=
  (L ((s3.afp (s3.effAnchor a)).headD 0)).alloc

/-- Smallest value of `f` over a list, starting from `m` (lowest-address rule, reference
realization). -/
def minOver (f : Nat → Nat) : Nat → List Nat → Nat
  | m, [] => m
  | m, l :: ls => minOver f (min m (f l)) ls

/-- `minOver` is at most the start and at most `f` on the list (lowest-address rule). -/
theorem minOver_le (f : Nat → Nat) :
    ∀ (ls : List Nat) (m : Nat), minOver f m ls ≤ m ∧ ∀ l ∈ ls, minOver f m ls ≤ f l
  | [], m => ⟨Nat.le_refl m, fun _ h => nomatch h⟩
  | l :: ls, m => by
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := minOver_le f ls (min m (f l))
    refine ⟨Nat.le_trans h1 (Nat.min_le_left _ _), fun l' hl' => ?_⟩
    rcases List.mem_cons.1 hl' with rfl | hl'
    · exact Nat.le_trans h1 (Nat.min_le_right _ _)
    · exact h2 l' hl'

/-- `minOver` is the start or a value of `f` on the list (lowest-address rule). -/
theorem minOver_mem (f : Nat → Nat) :
    ∀ (ls : List Nat) (m : Nat), minOver f m ls = m ∨ ∃ l ∈ ls, minOver f m ls = f l
  | [], m => .inl rfl
  | l :: ls, m => by
    simp only [minOver]
    rcases minOver_mem f ls (min m (f l)) with h | ⟨l', hl', h⟩
    · rw [h]
      rcases Nat.le_total m (f l) with hle | hle
      · exact .inl (Nat.min_eq_left hle)
      · exact .inr ⟨l, List.mem_cons_self .., Nat.min_eq_right hle⟩
    · exact .inr ⟨l', List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hl', h⟩

/-- Address of the reference to the region of authority `a` in `s2`: for a region whose leaves all
have zero physical size, the empty region included, the base of the allocation of the effective
anchor (§82.2, last sentence); otherwise the lowest address among the leaves of the region with a
nonzero size (lowest-address rule: a reference realization, not normative; the address of such a
region belongs to Spec 8, its width and encoding to Spec 11, §81). -/
def ptrAddr (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (s3 : S3) (a : Nat) : Nat :=
  match (s3.afp a).filter (fun l => decide (0 < (L l).len)) with
  | l :: ls => minOver (leafAddr s2 L) (leafAddr s2 L l) ls
  | [] => baseOf s2 (anchorAlloc L s3 a)

/-- The raw operation realizing `store(authority, target)` (§82.2, §82.3, §65): one write into the
range of the leaf `target` of the reference to the region of the authority, with the address of
`ptrAddr` and the provenance of the allocation of its effective anchor (§82.2). -/
def storeOps {Ty : Type} (pe : PtrEnc) (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (ty : Nat → Ty) (s3 : S3)
    (a p : Nat) : List (Machine.Op Ty) :=
  writeOps s2 L ty (fun _ => pe.enc (ptrAddr s2 L s3 a) (some (anchorAlloc L s3 a))) [p]

/-- The target of an `ok` `store` is a leaf of a usable place (§65.2). -/
theorem store_target {s3 : S3} {a p : Nat} (hpre : StorePre s3 a p) : LeafOfUsable s3 p :=
  ⟨p, List.mem_range.2 hpre.usable.lt, hpre.usable,
    mem_footprint.2 ⟨hpre.usable.lt, hpre.leaf, hpre.usable.lt, .inl rfl⟩⟩

/-- Realization of `store` (§82 preamble, §82.2, §82.3, §65, §16): under `Repr`, `WF3`, an `ok`
step of `store(authority, target)` and the parametric obligations of the write, the write of the
reference into the range of `target` is an `ok` raw step, and `Repr` holds after the step. Every
region has a reference address (§82.2). -/
theorem r6_store {Ty : Type} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}

recorded token compatible with itself (the automatic deallocation at `exitFrame` presents the
recorded token, §73, §82.5). -/
def ParamsOK {Ty : Type} (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (π : Params Ty) : Prop :=
  PlacementOK π.pl ∧ GeomOK π.geom ∧ ∀ r, C (π.rtok r) (π.rtok r)

/-- The raw operations realizing a kernel step from `s3`, the memory state being `s2` (§82
preamble; §82.2–§82.5): computed from the parameters and the two states, nothing chosen per
step. -/
def opsOf {Ty : Type} (π : Params Ty) : KOp → S3 → Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty)
  | .transfer src dst, s3, s2 => transferOps π.L π.ty s2 s3 src dst
  | .enter _ ls, s3, s2 => allocOps π.pl π.geom π.rtok s3.P.length s2 (rootIdx ls.toShape)
  | .exit, s3, _ => exitOps π.L π.rtok s3
  | .read _ ls, _, s2 => readOps s2 π.L π.ty ls
  | .write _ ls w, _, s2 => writeOps s2 π.L π.ty w ls
  | .writeShared _ ls w, _, s2 => writeOps s2 π.L π.ty w ls
  | .free p auth, _, _ => freeOps π.L p auth
  | .alloc _ _ ls, s3, s2 => allocOps π.pl π.geom π.rtok s3.P.length s2 (rootIdx ls.toShape)
  | .store a p, s3, s2 => storeOps π.pe s2 π.L π.ty s3 a p
  | _, _, _ => []

/-- Obligations of one step (§20.3, §82): the parametric obligations of its reads and writes
(§20.3, §15, §16); the layout of new places (`enterFrame`, `alloc`, §82.1, §23 `LayoutWF`); the
instantiation of `K.FreeCompat` on the deallocation compatibility of the machine (`free`, §80,
§70.2, §82.4). -/
def StepObl {Ty : Type} (k : K) (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty)
    (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) (π : Params Ty) (op : KOp) (s3 : S3) (s2 : Machine.State) :
    Prop :=
  OblAlong ObR ObW s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2) ∧
    match op with
    | .enter _ ls => NewLayout π.L (enterP s3 ls) s3.P.length s2.next π.geom (rootIdx ls.toShape)
    | .alloc _ ow ls => NewLayout π.L (allocP s3 ow ls) s3.P.length s2.next π.geom
        (rootIdx ls.toShape)
    | .free p auth => k.FreeCompat p auth → FreeCompatInst C π.rtok p auth
    | _ => True

/-- Realization of every kernel step (§82 preamble, R6): under the obligations of the parameters,
`Repr`, `WF3` and `NoDangling` (parts of the kernel invariant `KInv`, §57) and the obligations of
the step, the raw operations of the step form an execution of `ok` raw steps, and `Repr` holds
after the step. -/
theorem r6 {Ty : Type} {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {π : Params Ty} {op : KOp} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State}
    (hπ : ParamsOK C π) (hR : Repr π.L π.rtok s3 s2) (hw : WF3 s3) (hnd : NoDangling s3)
    (h : OpStep k op s3 s3') (hob : StepObl k C ObR ObW π op s3 s2) :
    Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (opsOf π op s3 s2) s2 (run s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2)) ∧
      Repr π.L π.rtok s3' (run s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2)) := by
  obtain ⟨hpl, hg, htc⟩ := hπ
  obtain ⟨hob, hx⟩ := hob
  cases op with
  | derive => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_derive hR h⟩
  | split => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_split hR h⟩
  | release => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_release hR h⟩
  | transfer => exact r6_transfer hR hw h hob
  | depend => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_depend hR h⟩
  | enter => exact r6_enter hR hw h hpl hg hx
  | exit =>
    have := r6_exit (ObR := ObR) (ObW := ObW) hR hw h htc
    exact ⟨this.1, this.2.2⟩
  | read =>
    have := r6_read (C := C) hR hw h hob
    exact ⟨this.1, this.2.2⟩
  | write => exact r2_write hR hw h hob
----
      have hnd := hw.frames.2.1
      have ht : s3.top ∈ s3.F.tail := hf
      unfold S3.top at ht
      cases hFe : s3.F with
      | nil => exact hF hFe
      | cons f F => rw [hFe] at ht hnd; exact (List.nodup_cons.1 hnd).1 ht
    | place hpl' _ ho' _ =>
      change s3.P[r]? = some _ at hpl'
      rw [hpl] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [ho] at ho'; cases ho'

/-- A leaf in the allocation of a root place belongs to that root place (§82.1, `inj`). -/
theorem Repr.leaf_of_alloc {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 : S3} {s2 : Machine.State}
    (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hw : WF3 s3) {l r : Nat} (hl : l < s3.P.length)
    (hlf : isLeaf s3.P l) (hr : RootPlace s3.P r) (he : (L l).alloc = (L r).alloc) :
    l ∈ footprint s3.P r := by
  obtain ⟨r', hr', hlr'⟩ := exists_rootPlace hw (l + 1) l (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hl
  have : r' = r := Decidable.of_not_not fun hne =>
    hR.inj r' r hr' hr hne (by rw [← hR.layout.alloc_part hlr', he])
  subst this
  exact mem_footprint.2 ⟨hl, hlf, hlr'⟩

/-- `pinned_address_stable` (§82.6, §74, §75; §63.5, §69.4, §70.4, §73.3): for every realized
kernel step (`r6`), a leaf covered by an active dynamic pinning obligation (§74: a leaf is pinned
while an active obligation covers it) or pinned by `K.Pinned`, whose allocation is live before the
step, keeps a live allocation and the same address after the raw operations of the step. The
memory machine never moves an allocation (§13); the content is that no deallocation of the step
touches a pinned leaf. -/
theorem pinned_address_stable {Ty : Type} {k : K} {π : Params Ty} {op : KOp}
    {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} (hR : Repr π.L π.rtok s3 s2) (hw : WF3 s3)
    (hnd : NoDangling s3) (h : OpStep k op s3 s3') {l : Nat} (hl : l < s3.P.length)
    (hlf : isLeaf s3.P l)
    (hpin : (∃ (o : Nat) (ob : PinOb), s3.pins[o]? = some ob ∧ ob.active = true ∧
      l ∈ ob.leaves) ∨ k.Pinned l)
    (hlive : LiveAlloc s2 (π.L l).alloc) :
    LiveAlloc (run s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2)) (π.L l).alloc ∧
      leafAddr (run s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2)) π.L l = leafAddr s2 π.L l := by
  have hwf := hR.adm.wf
  have haddr : leafAddr (run s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2)) π.L l = leafAddr s2 π.L l := by
    simp only [leafAddr]; rw [baseOf_run hwf _ (hlive.mono fun _ _ => trivial)]
  refine ⟨?_, haddr⟩
  have hnod : (∀ o ∈ opsOf π op s3 s2, NoDealloc o) →
      LiveAlloc (run s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2)) (π.L l).alloc :=
    fun hn => live_run _ _ hwf hn hlive
  have hpinned : ¬ (s3.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l) := fun ⟨h1, h2⟩ => by
    rcases hpin with h | h
    · rw [S3.pin_iff.2 h] at h1; cases h1
    · exact h2 h
  cases op with
  | transfer => exact hnod (copyOps_noDealloc _ _ _ _)
  | enter => exact hnod (allocOps_noDealloc _ _ _ _ _ _)
  | read =>

/-! ## Arena registry and the registries of live administrations (Spec 1 §46, §56) -/

/-- The arena registry (Spec 1 §46): library state separate from the kernel state and from the
synchronization registry (WC4 C2: library administration states remain separate from `S_C`). -/
abbrev ArenaReg := List Arena.ArenaEntry

/-- The synchronization registry as a registry of live administrations (Spec 1 §56; WC4 C13.7):
the `guarded` identities of its live entries. -/
def liveGuardeds (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : List Nat :=
  (reg.filter fun e => decide (e.Live s)).map (·.guarded)

/-! ## Derived operations (WC4 C13, C16–C18) -/

/-- The mutex value `M` of WC4 C12, C13: the immediate structural parent of the place `slot`
holding `guarded`. -/
def mutexOf (s : SC) (g : Nat) : Option Nat :=
  match (s.A[g]?).map (·.holder) with
  | some (Holder.place h) => parentOf s.P h
  | _ => none

/-- Preconditions of `newMutex(guarded)` executed by `c` (WC4 C13.1–C13.10), the arena registry
`ar` being the other registry of live administrations (Spec 1 §56). The interface and realization
obligations of WC4 C13 (C13.3, C13.6, initial physical controller state) are not represented: WC4
C13 says they "are not claimed to follow from the authority-only state `S_C`". -/
structure NewMutexPre (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) (ar : ArenaReg) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg)
    (c g : Nat) : Prop where
----
    Prop :=
  s.Live c ∧ ∃ e, reg[i]? = some e ∧ (s.view c).ExercisableAt e.guarded .modify ∧
    NoCoveringDesc s e.guarded ∧
    OptP (ControlOf L s e) (fun ctl => s.flat.Usable ctl ∧ isLeaf s.P ctl) False ∧
    st' = (s, reg.set i { e with grant := none })

/-! ## Derived arena operations executed by a context (Spec 1 §76–§78; WC4 C2, C19) -/

/-- Preconditions of `newArena(storage, internal)` executed by `c` (Spec 1 §76; WC4 C2): the
clauses of `Arena.NewArenaBase` on the view of `c`, §76.6 being read on the concurrent kernel state
(WC4 C2, C3, C20: `WF3` and `I1` over the globally live frames, `AnchorOrder` and
`AnchorOrderHeld` on `ancestorC`), and the guard of §76.4 over the arena registry and the
synchronization registry (Spec 1 §56: "all relevant registries of live administrations"; WC4
C13.7, OB-C16), with `Arena.Guard56`. -/
structure NewArenaPreC (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (ar : ArenaReg) (c storage internal : Nat) :
    Prop where
  /-- Spec 1 §76.1: `storage` is an existing, usable place. -/
  storageUsable : (s.view c).Usable storage
  /-- Spec 1 §76.1: `storage` is under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. -/
  storageRight : HasRight (s.view c) .modify storage
  /-- Spec 1 §76.2: `internal` exists, is active and has own mode `Modify`. -/
  internalAuth : OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.mode = .modify) False
  /-- Spec 1 §76.2: `ExercisableAt(s, internal, Modify)`. -/
  exercisable : (s.view c).ExercisableAt internal .modify
  /-- Spec 1 §76.3: `internal` is held by a place, the arena value. -/
  heldByPlace : OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => y.holder.isPlace = true) False
  /-- Spec 1 §76.3: `footprint(internal) ⊆ footprint(storage)`. -/
  fpSub : ∀ l ∈ s.flat.afp internal, l ∈ footprint s.P storage
  /-- Spec 1 §76.3: `footprint(storage) ⊆ footprint(internal)`. -/
  fpSup : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, l ∈ s.flat.afp internal
  /-- Spec 1 §76.5: all leaves of the arena value are already `Init`. -/
  valueInit : OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => Arena.LeavesInit s.flat y.holder) True
  /-- Spec 1 §76.6: `WF3` (§49) over the whole kernel state (WC4 C2, C20). -/
  wf3 : WF3 s.flat
  /-- Spec 1 §76.6: `I1` (§50) over the whole kernel state (WC4 C2). -/
  i1 : I1 s.flat
  /-- Spec 1 §76.6 re-indexed (WC4 C3): `AnchorOrder` (§44) on `ancestorC`. -/
  anchorOrder : AnchorOrderC s
  /-- Spec 1 §76.6 re-indexed (WC4 C3): `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44) on `ancestorC`. -/
  anchorOrderHeld : AnchorOrderHeldC s
  /-- Spec 1 §76.6: the new entry satisfies `ArenaInv` (§55). -/
  arenaInv : Arena.ArenaInv s.flat ⟨storage, internal, footprint s.P storage, []⟩
  /-- Spec 1 §76.4, §56 (WC4 C13.7, OB-C16): no live administration of the arena registry nor of
  the synchronization registry uses `internal`. -/
  guard : Arena.Guard56 [Arena.liveInternals s.flat ar, liveGuardeds s reg] internal

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `newArena` executed by `c` (Spec 1 §76). -/
instance (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (ar : ArenaReg) (c storage internal : Nat) :
    Decidable (NewArenaPreC s reg ar c storage internal) :=
  decidable_of_iff ((s.view c).Usable storage ∧ HasRight (s.view c) .modify storage ∧
    OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.mode = .modify) False ∧
    (s.view c).ExercisableAt internal .modify ∧
    OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => y.holder.isPlace = true) False ∧
    (∀ l ∈ s.flat.afp internal, l ∈ footprint s.P storage) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, l ∈ s.flat.afp internal) ∧
    OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => Arena.LeavesInit s.flat y.holder) True ∧
    WF3 s.flat ∧ I1 s.flat ∧ AnchorOrderC s ∧ AnchorOrderHeldC s ∧
    Arena.ArenaInv s.flat ⟨storage, internal, footprint s.P storage, []⟩ ∧
    Arena.Guard56 [Arena.liveInternals s.flat ar, liveGuardeds s reg] internal)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n, o⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n, o⟩,
     fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n, o⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n, o⟩⟩

/-- `newArena(storage, internal)` executed by `c` (Spec 1 §76, §58: `ok` or `reject`): the entry of
`Arena.newArenaEff` is registered; the kernel state and the synchronization registry are
unchanged (§76 `ok` effect). A context that is not live executes nothing. -/
def NewArenaStepC (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (ar : ArenaReg) (c storage internal : Nat)
    (o : Outcome3 (SC × ArenaReg)) : Prop :=
  s.Live c ∧ Guarded (NewArenaPreC s reg ar c storage internal)
    (s, ar ++ [⟨storage, internal, footprint s.P storage, []⟩]) o

/-- `issue(arena, region, destination)` of entry `i` executed by `c` (Spec 1 §77, §58; Part XIV: a
derived operation, on the pattern of `Arena.IssueD`): the static checks (§77.1, §77.2) and the
availability `fail` (§77.4) on the view of `c`; then `split` of `internal` on the region (O2) and
`store` of the block, of fresh identity `|A|`, into the destination (O8), both as executed by `c`
(`opStepC`; WC4 C2, C3: §65.4 and §65.5 read `ancestorC`); the metadata is updated on `ok`
(`Arena.issueMeta`). A context that is not live executes nothing. -/
inductive IssueStepC (k : K) (s : SC) (ar : ArenaReg) (c i : Nat) (region : List Nat)
    (dst : Nat) : Outcome3 (SC × ArenaReg) → Prop where
  | noEntry : s.Live c → ar[i]? = none → IssueStepC k s ar c i region dst .reject
  | static {E : Arena.ArenaEntry} : s.Live c → ar[i]? = some E →
      ¬ Arena.IssueStatic (s.view c) E region dst → IssueStepC k s ar c i region dst .reject
  | fail {E : Arena.ArenaEntry} : s.Live c → ar[i]? = some E →
      Arena.IssueStatic (s.view c) E region dst → ¬ Arena.Avail E region →
      IssueStepC k s ar c i region dst .fail
  | split {E : Arena.ArenaEntry} : ar[i]? = some E → Arena.IssueStatic (s.view c) E region dst →
      Arena.Avail E region → opStepC k (.split E.internal [region]) c s .reject →
      IssueStepC k s ar c i region dst .reject
  | store {E : Arena.ArenaEntry} {s₁ : SC} : ar[i]? = some E →
      Arena.IssueStatic (s.view c) E region dst → Arena.Avail E region →
      opStepC k (.split E.internal [region]) c s (.ok s₁) →
      opStepC k (.store s.A.length dst) c s₁ .reject → IssueStepC k s ar c i region dst .reject
  | ok {E : Arena.ArenaEntry} {s₁ s₂ : SC} : ar[i]? = some E →
      Arena.IssueStatic (s.view c) E region dst → Arena.Avail E region →
      opStepC k (.split E.internal [region]) c s (.ok s₁) →
      opStepC k (.store s.A.length dst) c s₁ (.ok s₂) →
      IssueStepC k s ar c i region dst (.ok (s₂, ar.set i (Arena.issueMeta s.flat E region)))

/-- `reset(arena)` of entry `i` executed by `c` (Spec 1 §78, §58; Part XIV): the derived operation
`Arena.ResetD` (`derive` of `internal` at `Modify` over the storage, `release`, the check of §78.3)
on the view of `c`, written back (WC4 C2); `derive` and `release` read neither `ancestor` nor the
stack beyond its top and its membership. A context that is not live executes nothing. -/
def ResetStepC (s : SC) (ar : ArenaReg) (c i : Nat) (o : Outcome3 (SC × ArenaReg)) : Prop :=
  s.Live c ∧ ∃ o₃, Arena.ResetD i ⟨s.view c, ar⟩ o₃ ∧
    o = omap (fun L' => (s.set L'.kern, L'.arenas)) o₃

/-- Writing back into `s` an `S3` whose stack is that of the view of `c`, then taking the view of
`c`, gives that `S3` back (WC4 C2). -/
theorem SC.view_set {s : SC} {c : Nat} {t : S3} (hF : t.F = (s.view c).F) :
    (s.set t).view c = t := by
  have h : (s.set t).view c = { t with F := (s.view c).F } := rfl
  rw [h, ← hF]

/-- Writing back twice keeps the second state only (WC4 C2). -/
theorem SC.set_set (s : SC) (t u : S3) : (s.set t).set u = s.set u := rfl

/-- An `ok` outcome of `newArena` executed by `c` (Spec 1 §76): the preconditions hold and the
entry is registered. -/
theorem newArenaStepC_ok {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c st i : Nat}
    {st' : SC × ArenaReg} (h : NewArenaStepC s reg ar c st i (.ok st')) :
    s.Live c ∧ NewArenaPreC s reg ar c st i ∧
      st' = (s, ar ++ [⟨st, i, footprint s.P st, []⟩]) :=
  ⟨h.1, Guarded.ok_iff.1 h.2⟩

/-- An `ok` outcome of `issue` executed by `c` (Spec 1 §77, Part XIV): the static checks and
availability, then `split` then `store` executed by `c`, then the metadata update. -/
theorem issueStepC_ok {k : K} {s : SC} {ar : ArenaReg} {c i : Nat} {region : List Nat}
    {dst : Nat} {st' : SC × ArenaReg} (h : IssueStepC k s ar c i region dst (.ok st')) :
    ∃ E s₁, ar[i]? = some E ∧ Arena.IssueStatic (s.view c) E region dst ∧
      Arena.Avail E region ∧ opStepC k (.split E.internal [region]) c s (.ok s₁) ∧
      opStepC k (.store s.A.length dst) c s₁ (.ok st'.1) ∧
      st'.2 = ar.set i (Arena.issueMeta s.flat E region) := by
  cases h with
  | ok hE hst hav hsp hsto => exact ⟨_, _, hE, hst, hav, hsp, hsto, rfl⟩

/-- An `ok` outcome of `reset` executed by `c` (Spec 1 §78, Part XIV): `derive` of `internal` at
`Modify` over the storage then `release` of the derived authority, both executed by `c` (WC4 C2),
the check of §78.3 holding, then the metadata update. -/
theorem resetStepC_ok {k : K} {s : SC} {ar : ArenaReg} {c i : Nat} {st' : SC × ArenaReg}
    (h : ResetStepC s ar c i (.ok st')) :
    ∃ E s₁, ar[i]? = some E ∧
      opStepC k (.derive E.internal (footprint s.P E.storage) .modify) c s (.ok s₁) ∧
      opStepC k (.release s.A.length) c s₁ (.ok st'.1) ∧ Arena.ResetNoDeps (s.view c) E ∧
      st'.2 = ar.set i (Arena.resetMeta s.flat E) := by
  obtain ⟨hl, o₃, hr, ho⟩ := h
  cases hr with
  | noEntry => cases ho
  | derive => cases ho
  | release => cases ho
  | contract => cases ho
  | @ok E t₁ t₂ hE hd hrl hnd =>
    cases ho
    have hF : t₁.F = (s.view c).F := by obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hd; rfl
    refine ⟨E, s.set t₁, hE, ⟨hl, .ok t₁, hd, rfl⟩, ?_, hnd, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨hl, .ok t₂, ?_, rfl⟩
    rw [SC.view_set hF]; exact hrl

/-- Separation of the two registries of live administrations (Spec 1 §56: "An authority identity
may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction"; WC4 C13.7, OB-C16): no
identity is at once the `guarded` of a live synchronization entry and the `internal` of a live
arena. -/
def AdminSep (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (ar : ArenaReg) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ reg, ∀ E ∈ ar, e.Live s → Arena.Live s.flat E → e.guarded ≠ E.internal

/-! ## Labelled steps, runs, encapsulation (WC4 C22, C23) -/

/-- Label of a step of the kernel with the synchronization library. -/
inductive Label where
  | kernel (c : Nat) (op : KernelOp)
  | spawn (c : Nat) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape)
  | terminate (c : Nat)
  | join (c d : Nat)
  | deriveSync (c g : Nat)
  | newMutex (c g : Nat)
  | acquire (c i : Nat)
  | unlock (c i : Nat)
  | resetLock (c i : Nat)
  | spawnVal (c : Nat) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape) (vs : List (Nat × Nat))
  | newArena (c storage internal : Nat)
  | issue (c arena : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat)
  | reset (c arena : Nat)

/-- Labelled `ok` step of the concurrent kernel with the synchronization and arena libraries
(WC4 C2, C4, C5, C6–C8, C13, C15–C18, C19; WC4 C23 for the by-value composite; Spec 1 §76–§78 for
the arenas): kernel and frame steps keep both registries; raw `deriveSync` runs under the library
instantiation of `SyncAuthorized` on the current registry (WC4 C14); the mutex operations change
the synchronization registry, the arena operations the arena registry (Spec 1 §46). -/
inductive LStep (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) :
    Label → SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg → SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg → Prop where
  | kernel {s s' : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c : Nat} {op : KernelOp} :
      opStepC k op c s (.ok s') → LStep k L (.kernel c op) (s, reg, ar) (s', reg, ar)
  | spawn {s s' : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c : Nat} {ps : List Nat}
      {ls : LocalShape} :
      SpawnStep s c ps ls (.ok s') → LStep k L (.spawn c ps ls) (s, reg, ar) (s', reg, ar)
  | terminate {s s' : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c : Nat} :
      TermStep k s c (.ok s') → LStep k L (.terminate c) (s, reg, ar) (s', reg, ar)
  | join {s s' : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c d : Nat} :
      JoinStep s c d (.ok s') → LStep k L (.join c d) (s, reg, ar) (s', reg, ar)
  | deriveSync {s s' : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c g : Nat} :
      DeriveSyncStep (libKC k L) reg s c g (.ok s') →
      LStep k L (.deriveSync c g) (s, reg, ar) (s', reg, ar)
  | newMutex {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c g : Nat} {st' : SC × SyncReg} :
      NewMutexOk k L ar s reg c g st' → LStep k L (.newMutex c g) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, st'.2, ar)
  | acquire {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c i : Nat} {st' : SC × SyncReg} :
      AcquireOk k L s reg c i st' → LStep k L (.acquire c i) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, st'.2, ar)
  | unlock {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c i : Nat} {st' : SC × SyncReg} :
      UnlockOk L s reg c i st' → LStep k L (.unlock c i) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, st'.2, ar)
  | resetLock {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c i : Nat} {st' : SC × SyncReg} :
      ResetLockOk L s reg c i st' → LStep k L (.resetLock c i) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, st'.2, ar)
  | spawnVal {s s' : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c : Nat} {ps : List Nat}
      {ls : LocalShape} {vs : List (Nat × Nat)} :
      SpawnValStep k s c ps ls vs (.ok s') →
      LStep k L (.spawnVal c ps ls vs) (s, reg, ar) (s', reg, ar)
  | newArena {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c st i : Nat} {st' : SC × ArenaReg} :
      NewArenaStepC s reg ar c st i (.ok st') →
      LStep k L (.newArena c st i) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, reg, st'.2)
  | issue {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c i : Nat} {region : List Nat} {dst : Nat}
      {st' : SC × ArenaReg} :
      IssueStepC k s ar c i region dst (.ok st') →
      LStep k L (.issue c i region dst) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, reg, st'.2)
  | reset {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c i : Nat} {st' : SC × ArenaReg} :
      ResetStepC s ar c i (.ok st') → LStep k L (.reset c i) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, reg, st'.2)

/-- WC4 C22.3 for the source `src` of a transfer in state `st`: for each live entry, `src` is
neither the place `slot` holding `guarded`, nor a strict structural subplace of `slot`, nor the
controller leaf `ctl`. -/
def TransferExcl (L : MutexLayout) (st : SC × SyncReg) (src : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ st.2, e.Live st.1 →
    OptP (slotOf st.1 e.guarded) (fun q => ¬ partOf st.1.P src q) True ∧
      ControlOf L st.1 e ≠ some src

/-- Decidability of `TransferExcl` (WC4 C22.3). -/

theorem LStep.labelled {k : K} {L L' : LState} (h : LStep k L L') : ∃ lop, LOpStep k lop L L' := by
  cases h with
  | kernel hk =>
    obtain ⟨op, h⟩ := kstep_labelled hk
    exact ⟨.kernel op, h, rfl⟩
  | newArena hs => exact ⟨.newArena _ _ _, hs⟩
  | issue hs => exact ⟨.issue _ _ _, hs⟩
  | reset hs => exact ⟨.reset _, hs⟩

/-- The kernel steps realizing a library operation from `L`, each with the kernel state it starts
from (Part XIV, §82.7): a kernel operation is its own step; `newArena` has none (§76: it registers
an administration without modifying the kernel); `issue` is `split` of `internal` on the region,
then `store` of the block, of fresh identity `|A|`, into the destination (§77); `reset` is
`derive` of `internal` at `Modify` over the storage, then `release` of the derived authority `|A|`
(§78). Without an entry, there is no step. -/
def kexp : LOp → LState → List (KOp × S3)
  | .kernel op, L => [(op, L.kern)]
  | .newArena .., _ => []
  | .issue i region dst, L => match L.arenas[i]? with
    | some E => [(.split E.internal [region], L.kern),
        (.store L.kern.A.length dst, splitEff L.kern E.internal [region])]
    | none => []
  | .reset i, L => match L.arenas[i]? with
    | some E => [(.derive E.internal (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify, L.kern),
        (.release L.kern.A.length,
          deriveEff L.kern E.internal (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify)]
    | none => []

/-- A sequence of `ok` kernel steps (§57, §58), each listed with the state it starts from. -/
inductive KPath (k : K) : S3 → List (KOp × S3) → S3 → Prop where
  | nil (s : S3) : KPath k s [] s
  | cons {op : KOp} {s s₁ s' : S3} {t : List (KOp × S3)} :
      OpStep k op s s₁ → KPath k s₁ t s' → KPath k s ((op, s) :: t) s'

/-- §82.7 (realization by O1–O16; Part XIV): every `ok` library step is the sequence of its
kernel steps `kexp`, from the kernel state before it to the kernel state after it. -/
section Trace

variable {Ty : Type}

/-- The raw operations realizing a sequence of kernel steps (§82 preamble, §20.3): the raw
operations `opsOf` of each step, in the memory state reached by the previous ones. -/
def ktrace (π : Params Ty) : List (KOp × S3) → Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty)
  | [], _ => []
  | (op, s3) :: t, s2 => opsOf π op s3 s2 ++ ktrace π t (run s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2))

/-- The raw operations realizing a library step (§82.7): those of its kernel steps. -/
def lopsOf (π : Params Ty) (lop : LOp) (L : LState) (s2 : Machine.State) : List (Machine.Op Ty) :=
  ktrace π (kexp lop L) s2

/-- The raw operations of composed kernel sequences are composed (§20.3 ¶3). -/
theorem ktrace_append (π : Params Ty) (t t' : List (KOp × S3)) (s2 : Machine.State) :
    ktrace π (t ++ t') s2 = ktrace π t s2 ++ ktrace π t' (run s2 (ktrace π t s2)) := by
  induction t generalizing s2 with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons p t ih =>
    obtain ⟨op, s3⟩ := p
    simp only [List.cons_append, ktrace, ih, run_append, List.append_assoc]

/-- The obligations of each kernel step of a sequence (§20.3, §82; `StepObl`), in the memory
state reached by the previous ones. -/
def KObl (k : K) (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty)
theorem reset_no_access_issued_reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} (hdd : DDSound k)
    (hst : StaticsOK statics) {L L₁ L₂ : LState} (hL : LReach k statics L) {i : Nat}
    {E : ArenaEntry} {t : List (LOp × LState)} (hE : L.arenas[i]? = some E)
    (hr : ResetD i L (.ok L₁)) (hp : LPath k L₁ t L₂) :
    ∀ e ∈ E.issued, e.1 ≠ [] → ∀ q ∈ ltrace t, usedAuth q.1 ≠ some e.2 := by
  have hlive : Live L.kern E := by
    cases hr with
    | @ok E' _ _ hE' hd _ _ =>
      rw [hE] at hE'; cases hE'
      exact (Guarded.ok_iff.1 hd).1.active
  exact reset_no_access_issued hE
    ((lReachNG_inv hdd hst hL.ng E (List.mem_of_getElem? hE)).2 hlive) hr hp

/-- §82.7 for translated library runs: the kernel steps of the derived operations are realized
by O1–O16 without reintroducing access after invalidation. The run is a labelled library run from
the initial library state; its memory state is reached from the initial memory state by the raw
operations of its kernel steps (the machine trace of the run is the trace of its kernel steps);
and after every legal `reset` in the run, no kernel step of the continuation uses an authority
derived from `internal` that covered a leaf of the administered storage, so no raw operation of
the continuation is an access through it.

The metadata (`available`, `issued`) is not realized: it is library state with no machine
realization in this model, so the "metadata" part of §82.7 is not covered. This is a reading,
recorded, not settled by the spec: §46 puts the entries in the library's abstract state, separate
from `S₃`, and §81 leaves the representation of library metadata to Spec 11; §36, §71.2 and §76.5
(with the last paragraph of §77) instead speak of metadata kept in storage (`SharedMutable`
storage updated by `writeShared`, provider metadata, the leaves of the arena value), which would
require raw writes realizing each metadata update. -/
theorem arena_realized {Ty : Type} {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {statics : Statics} {π : Params Ty} {L : LState}
    {s2 : Machine.State} (h : LSimRun k C ObR ObW statics π L s2) :
    ∃ t, LPath k (LState.init statics) t L ∧
      s2 = run (minit π statics) (ktrace π (ltrace t) (minit π statics)) ∧
      ∀ t₁ t₂ L₀ i E, t = t₁ ++ (.reset i, L₀) :: t₂ → L₀.arenas[i]? = some E →
        ∀ j, E.internal ∈ L₀.kern.ancs j →
          (∃ l ∈ L₀.kern.afp j, l ∈ footprint L₀.kern.P E.storage) →
          ∀ q ∈ ltrace t₂, usedAuth q.1 ≠ some j := by
  obtain ⟨t, hp, hs⟩ := h.trace
  refine ⟨t, hp, hs, ?_⟩
  rintro t₁ t₂ L₀ i E rfl hE j hj hc
  obtain ⟨L₁, hr, hp₂⟩ := LPath.split t₁ hp
  exact reset_no_access hE hr hp₂ hj hc

/-! ## A concrete library run (non-vacuity; §82.7, Part XIV) -/

section Dec

variable (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]
  {Ty : Type} (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) [DecidableRel C] (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty)
  (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) [∀ s o, Decidable (Obl ObR ObW s o)] (π : Params Ty)

/-- Decidability of the obligations of a kernel sequence (§20.3, §82). -/
instance kOblDec : (t : List (KOp × S3)) → (s2 : Machine.State) →
    Decidable (KObl k C ObR ObW π t s2)
  | [], _ => isTrue trivial
  | (op, s3) :: t, s2 =>
    @instDecidableAnd _ _ (stepOblDec k C ObR ObW π op s3 s2) (kOblDec t _)

end Dec

namespace Runs

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Examples Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement.Runs

/-- Memory state after the library operations `t`, each listed with the library state it starts
from, from the memory state `m` (§82.7). -/
def lrunM {Ty : Type} (π : Params Ty) : List (LOp × LState) → Machine.State → Machine.State
  | [], m => m
  | (lop, L) :: t, m => lrunM π t (run m (lopsOf π lop L m))
  | noArrival {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      Avail E region → IssueRight L.kern E region → ¬ IssueArrival L.kern E region dst →
      IssueC i region dst L .reject
  | ok {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      Avail E region → IssueRight L.kern E region → IssueArrival L.kern E region dst →
      IssueC i region dst L (.ok (issueL L i E region dst))

/-- `issue` as a derived operation (Part XIV, §77): its static checks, then the availability
`fail` (§77.4), then `split` of `internal` on the region (O2) and `store` of the block, of fresh
identity `|A|`, into the destination (O8); the metadata is updated on `ok`. -/
inductive IssueD (k : K) (i : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) (L : LState) :
    Outcome3 LState → Prop where
  | noEntry : L.arenas[i]? = none → IssueD k i region dst L .reject
  | static {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → ¬ IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      IssueD k i region dst L .reject
  | fail {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      ¬ Avail E region → IssueD k i region dst L .fail
  | split {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      Avail E region → SplitStep k E.internal [region] L.kern .reject →
      IssueD k i region dst L .reject
  | store {E : ArenaEntry} {s₁ : S3} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
      Avail E region → SplitStep k E.internal [region] L.kern (.ok s₁) →
      StoreStep L.kern.A.length dst s₁ .reject → IssueD k i region dst L .reject
  | ok {E : ArenaEntry} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : L.arenas[i]? = some E →
      IssueStatic L.kern E region dst → Avail E region →
      SplitStep k E.internal [region] L.kern (.ok s₁) →
      StoreStep L.kern.A.length dst s₁ (.ok s₂) →
      IssueD k i region dst L (.ok ⟨s₂, L.arenas.set i (issueMeta L.kern E region)⟩)

/-! ## O19 `reset` (§78) -/

/-- §78.3 (v0.1): no still-usable place depends on an anchor in the strict origin subtree of
`internal` that covers a leaf of the administered storage. Dependencies of contained values are
covered since parts are places. -/
def ResetNoDeps (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, E.internal ∈ s.ancs x →
    ∀ l ∈ s.afp x, l ∉ footprint s.P E.storage

/-- Decidability of `ResetNoDeps` (§78.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Decidable (ResetNoDeps s E) := by
  unfold ResetNoDeps; infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `reset(arena)` (§78). "`internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain
valid" (§78.1) and "validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied" (§78.3) name no
checkable condition beyond `ArenaInv` and are not represented. -/
structure ResetPre (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop where
  /-- §78.1: the entry is live. -/
  live : s.Active E.internal
  /-- §78.1: `MetaRight`, exercisable `Modify` over the arena value (§36). -/
  metaRight : MetaRight s E
  /-- §78.2: no active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the storage. -/
  noCover : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, E.internal ∈ s.ancs j → s.Active j →
    ∀ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∉ footprint s.P E.storage
  /-- §78.3: no usable place depends on an anchor in the strict origin subtree of `internal`
  covering a leaf of the storage. -/
  noDeps : ResetNoDeps s E

/-- Decidability of `ResetPre` (§78). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Decidable (ResetPre s E) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.Active E.internal ∧ MetaRight s E ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, E.internal ∈ s.ancs j → s.Active j →
      ∀ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∉ footprint s.P E.storage) ∧ ResetNoDeps s E)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩⟩

/-- Kernel part of the effect of `reset` (§78 `ok` effect, Part XIV): the record of the `Modify`
derivation of `internal` over all the storage, already released; no leaf becomes `Init`. -/
def resetKEff (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : S3 :=
  { s with A := s.A ++ [⟨.modify, some E.internal, footprint s.P E.storage, .frame s.top, false⟩] }

/-- Metadata part of the effect of `reset` (§78 `ok` effect, §46): all leaves of the storage
become available; `issued` is cleared. -/
def resetMeta (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : ArenaEntry :=
  { E with available := footprint s.P E.storage, issued := [] }

/-- Library state after an `ok` reset of entry `i` (§78). -/
def resetL (L : LState) (i : Nat) (E : ArenaEntry) : LState :=
  ⟨resetKEff L.kern E, L.arenas.set i (resetMeta L.kern E)⟩

/-- The contract of `reset` on entry `i` (§78, §58): `ok` when the entry exists and the
preconditions hold, `reject` otherwise. -/
inductive ResetC (i : Nat) (L : LState) : Outcome3 LState → Prop where
  | noEntry : L.arenas[i]? = none → ResetC i L .reject
  | reject {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → ¬ ResetPre L.kern E → ResetC i L .reject
  | ok {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → ResetPre L.kern E →
      ResetC i L (.ok (resetL L i E))

/-- `reset` as a derived operation (Part XIV, §78): `derive` of `internal` at `Modify` over the
footprint of the storage (O1), `release` of the derived authority (O3), then the explicit contract
check of §78.3; the metadata is updated on `ok`. -/
inductive ResetD (i : Nat) (L : LState) : Outcome3 LState → Prop where
  | noEntry : L.arenas[i]? = none → ResetD i L .reject
  | derive {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E →
      DeriveStep E.internal (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify L.kern .reject →
      ResetD i L .reject
  | release {E : ArenaEntry} {s₁ : S3} : L.arenas[i]? = some E →
      DeriveStep E.internal (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify L.kern (.ok s₁) →
      ReleaseStep L.kern.A.length s₁ .reject → ResetD i L .reject
  | contract {E : ArenaEntry} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : L.arenas[i]? = some E →
      DeriveStep E.internal (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify L.kern (.ok s₁) →
      ReleaseStep L.kern.A.length s₁ (.ok s₂) → ¬ ResetNoDeps L.kern E → ResetD i L .reject
  | ok {E : ArenaEntry} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : L.arenas[i]? = some E →
      DeriveStep E.internal (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify L.kern (.ok s₁) →
      ReleaseStep L.kern.A.length s₁ (.ok s₂) → ResetNoDeps L.kern E →
      ResetD i L (.ok ⟨s₂, L.arenas.set i (resetMeta L.kern E)⟩)

/-! ## Helper lemmas (§40, §42, §43, §65) -/

/-- `Allows` at `Modify` is effective `Modify` (§43). -/
theorem allows_modify_iff {e : Option Mode} : Allows e .modify ↔ e = some .modify := by
  cases e with
  | none => simp [Allows, OptP]
  | some m => cases m <;> simp [Allows, OptP, Mode.le]

/-- Effective `Modify` permits every requested mode (§43: `Observe ≤ Modify`). -/
theorem allows_some_modify (m : Mode) : Allows (some .modify) m := by
  cases m <;> simp [Allows, OptP, Mode.le]

/-- R5 for the arena operations (WC4 C24; Spec 1 §82.7): on a single-context state, the
realization of `newArena`, `issue` and `reset` executed by the context is the realization
`RefinementArena.lopsOf` of the corresponding library operation on the projection. -/
theorem r5_arena {Ty : Type} (π : Refinement.Params Ty) (w : Nat → Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat)
    {s : SC} (hs : s.Single) (ar : ArenaReg) (m : Machine.State) (others : List (List Nat))
    (st i dst : Nat) (region : List Nat) :
    realize π w (.newArena 0 st i) s ar m =
        RefinementArena.lopsOf π (.newArena others st i) ⟨s.toS3, ar⟩ m ∧
      realize π w (.issue 0 i region dst) s ar m =
        RefinementArena.lopsOf π (.issue i region dst) ⟨s.toS3, ar⟩ m ∧
      realize π w (.reset 0 i) s ar m = RefinementArena.lopsOf π (.reset i) ⟨s.toS3, ar⟩ m := by
  have hv := single_view hs
  refine ⟨rfl, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp only [realize, RefinementArena.lopsOf, RefinementArena.kexp]
    cases ar[i]? with
    | none => rfl
    | some E =>
      dsimp only
      rw [SC.view_set (s := s) (c := 0) (t := splitEff (s.view 0) E.internal [region]) rfl, hv]
      simp [RefinementArena.ktrace, kopOf]
      rfl
  · simp only [realize, RefinementArena.lopsOf, RefinementArena.kexp]
    cases ar[i]? with
    | none => rfl
    | some E =>
      dsimp only
      rw [SC.view_set (s := s) (c := 0)
        (t := deriveEff (s.view 0) E.internal (footprint s.P E.storage) .modify) rfl, hv]
      simp [RefinementArena.ktrace, kopOf, opsOf]

end Ern.Concurrency

content.content:
## 65. O8 — Controlled Storage of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active, **derived**, and held by the current frame; a root authority can never be stored by `store`.
2. `target` is a usable **leaf** under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It holds no other **active** authority. Its data already being `Init` does not by itself prohibit the operation.
3. The stored authority covers neither a leaf of `target` nor the leaves of storage transitively owned by it.
4. The effective anchor of `authority` respects `AnchorOrder` relative to the frame of `target`; other dependencies are preserved.
5. **In the resulting state**, `target` remains under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame (`store_keeps_target_reachable`), and `AnchorOrderHeld` remains true. This is a genuine additional precondition, not an automatic consequence of the preceding ones.

**`ok` effect:** The holder of `authority` becomes `target`; the authority is added to `D(target)`; **only** leaf `target` becomes `Init`. Other fields of a structure, even adjacent ones, do not change their initialization state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Overwriting an active authority already held by the leaf is prohibited; its explicit release may make the target reusable. The resulting-state clause does not by itself prohibit all cycles possible after other operations: general freedom from blocking (`NoLock`) is not adopted here.

----
## 73. O7 — Exiting a Frame

**Preconditions**

1. The current frame is not the initial frame and has a surviving caller.
2. Results that must survive have already been legally transferred to their destinations; no active authority or dependency may remain invalidly attached to locals that are about to die.
3. **No leaf of a place that dies with the frame, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`).
4. Iterated reanchoring of surviving authorities and anchors reaches the **first surviving active origin**, held either by a surviving frame or by a usable place whose terminal owner survives; it is not permitted to skip a surviving origin merely because it is held by a place. The operation is rejected when no suitable surviving origin exists, particularly if the chain reaches a root of the exiting frame.
5. Validity of anchors of surviving values and `AnchorOrderHeld` are checked **in the resulting state**. Other state invariants and resource contracts are respected.

**`ok` effect:**

- the current frame is removed from the stack; its untransferred locals and substorages dying with them become unusable;
- authorities still held by that frame, or by places that have become unusable, are released;
- origins of surviving derived authorities are reanchored to the **first surviving active origin** of their chains, whether held by a frame or a usable place, and the `D` anchors of surviving values are correspondingly reanchored;
- reanchoring changes **neither the footprint nor the own mode** of an authority; parameter identities and relations specific to the frame cease their operational role;
- the calling frame becomes current again.

**Other outcome:** `reject`. Exiting does not entail automatic physical deallocation of all dead places. Deferred cleanup (`defer`) lies outside this kernel. Reanchoring may change the current `origin` relation; protection of a historical borrow lineage during an invocation is a distinct, deferred question.

# XIII. Pinning, Statics, and External Commitments

Pinning forbids certain movements or ends of lifetime. It is not a general guarantee of content immutability.

## 74. O15 — Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over the relevant leaves, and the operation respects applicable pinning obligations.

**`ok` effect:** A dynamic pinning obligation of fresh identity is installed on the relevant leaves. A leaf is dynamically pinned while at least one active pinning obligation covers it. While an obligation is active, `transfer`, `endUse`, `free`, and `exitFrame` are rejected if they act on leaves it pins; removal of this obligation requires `unpin` under `K.ExternalDone`. Pinning does not make contents immutable. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 75. O16 — Removal of Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `unpin` designates one active dynamic pinning obligation, installed by `pin` on `place`; `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify`, and contract `K.ExternalDone`, applied to that obligation, attests that all relevant external use has ended.

**`ok` effect:** The designated dynamic pinning obligation ends, and only that one: a leaf it covered stays pinned while another active obligation covers it. The step does not itself modify values, their initialization, or their access authorities. Static obligations are not removed by this operation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

**Associated static rule (`StaticPinnedBottom`):** Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places **directly** owned by the **base frame**, not merely transitively owned by a static value. This restriction ensures that they do not die when an intermediate frame exits.

# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction

An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.

## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena

**Preconditions**

1. `storage` is an existing, usable place under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It may be local, static, allocated, or a block issued by a previous arena.
2. `internal` is explicitly named by the caller, exists, is active, has own mode `Modify`, and `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` holds.
3. `internal` is **held by a place**: that place is the arena value; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
5. All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are already `Init`; construction does not initialize them implicitly.
6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect, in the resulting state, `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, and `AnchorOrderHeld` over the whole kernel state, and the new entry satisfies `ArenaInv` (Section 55).

**`ok` effect:** A live entry `{storage, internal, available, issued}` is added; the initial `available` set represents the administered storage, and `issued` is initially empty. Registering the entry fabricates no place, access right, or `Init` state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.

## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block

**Static preconditions**

1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
2. `region` belongs to the administered storage; `destination` is a usable **leaf** holding no active authority; the destination can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. The fact that `destination` is already `Init` is not in itself grounds for rejection, in accordance with O8.2.
   **Local self-blocking prevention: leaf `destination` is not in `region`, including when the region is declared available.** This condition is static and is checked before an availability `fail`.
3. Applicable **static** validity and non-escape restrictions for the destination are satisfied. The `AnchorOrder` check depending on the new anchor is performed on the **simulated resulting state**, after the availability check described in point 4; it cannot turn an unavailable issuance (`fail`) into `reject`.

**Availability and exercisability checks**

4. If static conditions hold but **at least one leaf of `region` does not belong to `available`**, the operation produces **`fail` and leaves the entire state unchanged**. The empty region is always available. An unavailable region does not permit a prior static rejection to be bypassed.
5. If the region is available, the effective mode of `internal` on that region must permit `Modify`; otherwise the outcome is `reject`.
6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.

**`ok` effect:** A block authority of fresh identity, derived from `internal` and of mode `Modify`, is issued for the region; it is held by `destination`, which receives the corresponding anchor. The leaves of the region leave `available`, and the issuance is added to `issued` with its authority. **Only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`**; no other leaf of the arena value changes initialization. Previous issuances remain intact and valid. Issuance does not automatically install anchors on third-party values: they must use their lawful dependency mechanisms.

**Outcomes:** `ok`, `fail` (region unavailable after static validation), `reject` (static rule, effective right, or anchoring not satisfied). The destination may be a leaf of the arena value itself: its initialization then constitutes **an explicit write to that destination**, not implicit initialization of the entire arena value's metadata.

## 78. O19 — Collective Arena Reset

**Preconditions**

1. The entry exists and is live. **`MetaRight(s,arena)` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value**, in accordance with Section 36. `writeShared` over metadata alone, even when legal, does not replace such exercise. `internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain valid.
2. **No active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the administered storage.** A derived authority with an empty footprint does not, by itself, block `reset`.
3. No still-usable place depends, directly or transitively, on an anchor in the **strict origin subtree of `internal`** (`internal` itself is excluded) that covers a leaf of the administered storage. Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active descendants covering the storage, and remains explicit in the abstraction contract. Validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** All **leaves** of the administered storage become available again, and the issuance list is cleared under the arena contract. No still-active derived authority covering those leaves may remain, by precondition 2; an empty-footprint derivative may remain active without designating any recycled leaf. **No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`**, including in the arena value. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Safe reuse after `reset` requires that previous issuances **covering recycled leaves**, and the dependencies on which their validity rests, have effectively ceased preventing their reuse. Any active empty-footprint derivatives cover none of those leaves. A historically issued region does not remain permanently unavailable solely for that reason.

# XV. Transitive Dependencies, Returns, and Value Behavior

Dependent values may survive transfers and calls only if the required anchors and rights remain valid. Second-class access does not imply an arbitrary persistent reference.

## 79. Non-Escaping Values and Returns

The second-class nature of access authorities does not prohibit constructing a value carrying a derived authority or returning a result dependent on a caller-owned resource. What is prohibited is artificially extending the validity of a local origin.

A typical scenario is:

```text
arena = create_arena()
buffer = create_buffer(arena)
use(buffer)
endUse(buffer)       // or equivalent release of its dependent rights
----
## 82. Representation Relation and Concrete Obligations

1. **Places and bytes:** relate `P`, `footprint` leaves, their ownership, and their parts to the storage units, offsets, ranges, identities, and alignment constraints of the elementary memory machine; establish actual disjointness for `DeclaredDisjoint` declarations.
2. **Authorities and operations:** connect effective modes and `ExercisableAt` to concrete read, write, and pointer-validity conditions; show that safe access governed by Parts VI through XV satisfies the obligations of Part III, without conflating ownership and binary representation. A pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size is represented like a pointer to the empty region: its address is the base of the allocation of the effective anchor of its authority, and that allocation is its provenance.
3. **Initialization:** relate `Uninit`, `Init`, and `Moved` to concrete values and representations; an authority `store` must correspond to writing an actual reference into **a single logical leaf** with an appropriate representation.
4. **Allocation and deallocation:** relate `alloc` / `free` to `AllocStep` / `DeallocStep`, justify `Satisfiable`, `Deallocable`, and `FreeCompat`, as well as the zero-physical-size case.
5. **Lifetimes:** relate `endUse`, `exitFrame`, `NoDangling`, dependencies, and death markers to the validity effects on actual storage.
6. **Pinning and static storage:** prove compatibility of permitted moves and pinned-address restrictions; specify the physical obligations of statics and external use. Hardware-specific MMIO semantics remain outside the sequential kernel.
7. **Arenas:** show that the library abstraction's derived operations and metadata, distinct from `S₃`, can be realized by operations O1–O16; relate issued regions and local/static/allocated storage to the elementary memory machine without reintroducing access after invalidation.
8. **`noalias`:** infer no pointer-lowering property from abstract invariants alone; memory justification is established here and the translation choices at Spec 13 level.

# XVIII. Examples of Semantic Behavior

The fragments below are **traces of abstract operations**, not language syntax. The judgments illustrate normative rules; they create no exception to the detailed preconditions.

## 83. Address Reuse and Old Provenance

An allocation `a` is created and an access retains its provenance; after deallocation, a new allocation `b` may occupy the same address. `a ≠ b` as abstract identities: reading through the old access is invalid even if the addresses are equal. A new valid access with provenance `b` may be used within its rights.

## 84. Partial Initialization and Reading

A valid write to a subrange initializes its corresponding bytes. Reading another subrange that remains uninitialized is not permitted. The correspondence for logical state `Init` must guarantee a representation valid for the expected type; the mere presence of bits does not authorize type confusion.

## 85. Splitting a Structure or SoA Columns

Starting from a `Modify` authority exercised over a structure, `split` may provide `Modify` authorities over disjoint leaf regions. Modification of each region is permitted as long as the other validity and holder conditions hold; a second independent derivation over the same leaf does not become legal merely by having a distinct name.

## 86. Arena, Active Views, and Reset

Two disjoint issued regions may be used simultaneously with valid derived rights. `reset` is rejected while an issuance or active dependency would make recycling unsafe; after a legal end of use for all the relevant blocks, the region may be reissued. Reissuance modifies neither the bytes nor the initialization state. A read remains subject to the ordinary conditions of the memory model, notably `Init`, access rights, and representation validity for the requested type. Spec 4 will determine the construction and typing obligations of reissued values.

## 87. Pinning an In-Place Value

A pinned in-place leaf cannot be physically moved by `transfer`. If only an allocation owned by a value is pinned, transfer of that value may remain valid when the other conditions hold, because the owned allocation is not physically moved.

## 88. Local Self-Blocking and Indirect Cycles

An authority stored by `transfer` in a place that would then become its new holder cannot cover any leaf of that place. Likewise, `issue` cannot issue into a leaf belonging to the issued region, **or into a destination that would no longer be exercisable in `Modify` in the resulting state** (O8.5). These restrictions do not promise general freedom from authority cycles: indirect blocking compatible with safety may remain.

## 89. Handles and Persistent References

In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.

## 90. Global and Called Frame

Global storage is anchored to the base frame, but a called function does not acquire ambient authority to modify it merely by being invoked. To access a global, it receives a derived authority under `enterFrame` conditions and may exercise only its effective modes.

content.content:
## C2. Concurrent State and External Contracts

The candidate concurrent authority machine is:

\[ S_C=(C,F_C,P,I,A,D) \]

where:

- `C` identifies execution contexts and their lifecycle states.
- `F_C` contains their local frame stacks and extended frame-parent relation.
- `P`, `I`, `A`, and `D` retain their meanings from Spec 1.

The authority and dependency state is globally coherent. Library administration states, including synchronization registries, remain separate from `S_C`.

The concurrency specification introduces an external contract extension `K_C` with a projection to the unchanged Spec 1 contract `K`. A synchronization registry may be supplied as an **external argument** to `K_C.SyncAuthorized` by the reference abstraction. It does not become a component of `S_C`. This is the candidate P2 convention, subject to formal verification of its state-dependent soundness.

For an inherited operation executed by context `c`, all occurrences of “the current frame” refer to the top of the live local stack of `c`. References to live frames, usable places, ownership chains, authority holders and orphan conditions range over the globally live frame structure. An inherited `K.Satisfiable` obligation for a context-executed allocation is evaluated on the `S₃` view of the executing context (`SC.view(s,c)` in the exploratory model); this is candidate P1 and must preserve the soundness requirements of Spec 1's unchanged `K`.

For a single context with no active concurrent mechanism, these interpretations and the projection of `K_C` must coincide with Spec 1.

## C3. Frame Ancestry — H1

Each live context has a nonempty local stack.

Frame identities are globally unique.

The initial context contains the base frame of Spec 1, which never exits.

----
## C24. Sequential Conservativity

For corresponding single-context states and inherited operations O1–O16:

- preconditions and outcomes coincide;
- projected effects coincide;
- authority exercise retains the Spec 1 definition;
- sequential ancestry is recovered;
- the applicable sequential invariants are preserved.

The reachable sequential domain under inherited operations must correspond to the sequential domain of Spec 1 under the stated state correspondence.

A transition history involving additional contexts must not return to an invalid single-context authority state.

## C25. Abstract-to-Concrete Realization Obligations

The abstract machine imposes no universal runtime authority metadata. The synchronization library may maintain justified implementation metadata; the frozen Spec 1 §4 does not forbid it.

A sound implementation of the reference mutex must prove correspondence between the external registry and physical controller, preserve `ControlOf` under legal whole-value transfers, and enforce safe-interface encapsulation including C22.1–5. In particular, the prohibition of `endUse` on `ctl` or a strict structural subplace of `slot` is an interface property; the unchanged kernel O12 remains available to programs outside that abstraction contract.

Successful controller acquisition must imply the remaining `deriveSync` obligations through proven state invariants and contractual authorization facts. For the reference mutex, authorization is instantiated using **only** the entry's liveness, grant availability and the requesting frame's controller access. Its proof may use the global kernel invariants and the synchronization invariants but may not place its desired conclusion inside the definition of `SyncAuthorized`.

The ambition to check only the physical lock word at runtime is a reference optimization target, not a universal requirement of Spec 1. The exact atomicity, event-ordering and data-race obligations are deferred to `OB-C01`–`OB-C06`, with controller realization specifically under `OB-C05`.

---

# IV. Open Obligations

| ID | Obligation |
|---|---|
| `OB-C01` | Concurrent event model and definition of permitted executions |
| `OB-C02` | Conflict relations, synchronizes-with relations, and `happens-before` |
| `OB-C03` | Atomic operations, memory orders, and permitted observations |
| `OB-C04` | `LockOrder` for successive protected critical sections |
| `OB-C05` | Atomic realization and correspondence of synchronized acquisition, unlock, and recovery |
| `OB-C06` | Data-race freedom for all permitted safe executions |
| `OB-C07` | Type-system rules for cross-context transferability and shareability — Spec 4 |
| `OB-C08` | Encapsulation and library contract enforcement — Specs 4 and 10 |
| `OB-C09` | Final by-value passing conventions, cancellation, abnormal termination, and cleanup — Spec 3 |
| `OB-C10` | External execution contexts and interoperability — Spec 11 |
| `OB-C11` | Event-order consequences of `join`, completion, and frame-exit protocols |
| `OB-C12` | Concrete correspondence and refinement obligations of Spec 1 §82 |

/-! ## O8 `store` re-indexed (Spec 1 §65) -/

/-- Effect of `store` executed by `c` (Spec 1 §65 effect, WC4 C2). -/
def storeEffC (s : SC) (c a p : Nat) : SC := s.set (storeEff (s.view c) a p)

/-- Preconditions of `store` executed by `c` (Spec 1 §65 re-indexed, WC4 C2). -/
structure StorePreC (s : SC) (c a p : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- Spec 1 §65.1: the authority is active, derived, and held by the current frame. -/
  derivedHeld : OptP ((s.view c).A[a]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.origin ≠ none ∧
    y.holder = .frame (s.view c).top) False
  /-- Spec 1 §65.2: `target` is usable. -/
  usable : (s.view c).Usable p
  /-- Spec 1 §65.2: `target` is a leaf. -/
  leaf : isLeaf (s.view c).P p
  /-- Spec 1 §65.2: exercisable `Modify` over `target`. -/
  right : HasRight (s.view c) .modify p
  /-- Spec 1 §65.2: `target` holds no active authority. -/
  free : ∀ j ∈ List.range (s.view c).A.length,
    OptP ((s.view c).A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place p) True
  /-- Spec 1 §65.3: the authority covers no leaf of `target` nor of storage it owns. -/
  noCover : ∀ l ∈ (s.view c).afp a, l ∉ footprint (s.view c).P p ∧
    ∀ q ∈ List.range (s.view c).P.length, OwnedIn (s.view c).P p q →
      l ∉ footprint (s.view c).P q
  /-- Spec 1 §65.4 re-indexed: the effective anchor respects `AnchorOrder` (on `ancestorC`)
  relative to the frame of `target`. -/
  anchorOrder : EffAnchorOKC s a ((s.view c).pframe p)
/-- Preconditions of `exitFrameC` executed by `c` (Spec 1 §73 re-indexed; WC4 C6, C6.1: O7.1
transposed, O7.2–O7.5 on the global state). The surviving frames are the other globally live
frames. -/
structure ExitPreC (k : K) (s : SC) (c : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- Spec 1 §73.1 re-indexed (WC4 C6, first paragraph): the current frame of `c` is not the
  initial frame of its context and has a surviving caller in its stack. -/
  hasCaller : (s.stk c).tail ≠ []
  /-- Spec 1 §73.2, §73.4, §73.5: every anchor of a place usable after the exit has a surviving
  authority among itself and its origins. -/
  anchors : ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, ({ s.view c with F := (s.view c).F.tail } : S3).Usable q →
    ∀ x ∈ s.D q, firstSurv (s.view c) (s.view c).F.tail (x :: (s.view c).ancs x) ≠ none
  /-- Spec 1 §73.4: every surviving derived authority has a surviving active origin. -/
  origins : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, Survives (s.view c) (s.view c).F.tail a →
    (s.view c).org a ≠ none → firstSurv (s.view c) (s.view c).F.tail ((s.view c).ancs a) ≠ none
  /-- Spec 1 §73.3: no leaf of a place that dies with the frame is pinned. -/
  notPinned : ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (s.view c).Usable q →
    ¬ ({ s.view c with F := (s.view c).F.tail } : S3).Usable q →
    ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, (s.view c).pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l
  /-- Spec 1 §73.5 re-indexed: `AnchorOrderHeld` (on `ancestorC`) in the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrderHeld : AnchorOrderHeldC (exitEffC s c)

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `exitFrameC` (Spec 1 §73). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : SC) (c : Nat) : Decidable (ExitPreC k s c) :=
  decidable_of_iff ((s.stk c).tail ≠ [] ∧
    (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, ({ s.view c with F := (s.view c).F.tail } : S3).Usable q →
      ∀ x ∈ s.D q, firstSurv (s.view c) (s.view c).F.tail (x :: (s.view c).ancs x) ≠ none) ∧
    (∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, Survives (s.view c) (s.view c).F.tail a →
      (s.view c).org a ≠ none → firstSurv (s.view c) (s.view c).F.tail ((s.view c).ancs a) ≠ none) ∧
    (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (s.view c).Usable q →
      ¬ ({ s.view c with F := (s.view c).F.tail } : S3).Usable q →
      ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, (s.view c).pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l) ∧
    AnchorOrderHeldC (exitEffC s c))

/-! ## The inherited operations O1–O16 executed by a context (WC4 C2) -/

/-- Outcome relation of a kernel operation O1–O16 executed by context `c` (Spec 1 §60–§75
re-indexed, WC4 C2). Operations reading `ancestor` or changing the stack have their re-indexed
preconditions and effects; the others run on the view of `c`. A context that is not live executes
nothing. -/
def opStepC (k : K) : KernelOp → Nat → SC → Outcome3 SC → Prop
  | .transfer src dst, c, s, o =>
    s.Live c ∧ Guarded (TransferPreC k s c src dst) (transferEffC s c src dst) o
  | .depend q x, c, s, o => s.Live c ∧ Guarded (DependPreC s c q x) (dependEffC s c q x) o
  | .store a p, c, s, o => s.Live c ∧ Guarded (StorePreC s c a p) (storeEffC s c a p) o
